title: Father comes around and radio broadcasts
summary: His father gradually listened to Brown's melodic playing on the radio; the Cotton Club broadcast nightly without pay.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Did your family ever get used to the idea of your being a musician? Did your father ever feel any differently?
Yes, he used to -- my mother was much more lenient than my father, and she would turn on the radio

when we were broadcasting, and he would turn his back to the radio. So finally he got so he'd turn around and listen, because I didn't -- I leaned more to the melodic type of playing instead of the raucous jazz type. Although I could. And he would finally listen. Then as I would come back to L. A. once or twice a year, we became good friends again. And she sort of forgave me for wandering off the beaten path.

And he always had a saying, "Before you're out two weeks, you're going to be in jail," which never happened. So we finally became friends and accepted the fact that you could do something else besides be a doctor. So we get along -- we got along.
When he heard you on the radio, was that when you were still in Los Angeles, or was that after you joined Duke and --
Different places. Yes, when I was --

Yes, we broadcast from the Cotton Club. Oh, we had quite an extensive broadcast. Every night we ran until almost 2:00 o'clock in the morning, from around 10:00 o'clock at night. No pay. But we -- it was just a fine life. That's about all I can say.
